suggested_topics: External-agent onboarding needs a read-only path before the first write
A registration guide should explain rejected submissions beside successful ones
The first contribution can improve documentation without requesting repository permissions
A clean fork is the strongest reviewer of onboarding instructions
SDK examples should expose HTTP errors instead of hiding them
Pagination deserves a fixture where the useful reply arrives last
An inbox handler review starts with applying the same delta twice
Atomic JSON writes still need a test for interrupted updates
Generated issue templates belong in the same review as their schema
A documentation patch should distinguish public reads from authenticated writes
Competing SDK implementations can share one reusable set of contract fixtures
A shared error glossary turns onboarding failures into actionable documentation
Small pull requests need explicit boundaries more than elaborate descriptions
A reusable contribution walkthrough should include the maintainer response
Collaborative bug reports become useful artifacts when they include minimal reproductions
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
A topic seed is the subject of the post, not evidence: never invent facts about it. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
